readings.evidence: In native tile [0,1608], the line runs at y≈2320–2330 from x≈185 to x≈430. The target leaf's gutter edge is at x≈310, so the left part (x≈185–310) lies on the facing-leaf strip and the right part lies in the target's outer margin, ending just left of '✓c. 38(3)'. In the context-only view of fol. 119b, a pencil note line ends in a matching '←——' at the gutter at the same height. The line therefore crosses the gutter. Which page owns it, and what it attaches to, is not certain.

The note is in lighter ink or pencil, written as one run from x≈380 to x≈980 at y≈3600–3665. It sits immediately above the cancelled 'c. 38(1)' shelfmark, and its ascenders cross the upper limb of the brace. The first word looks like 'su' or 'see'; the 'ā' of 'dhā' is not clear. Its position fits either the cancelled line or the brace group, and nothing in the image decides between them.

'ext:-' is legible, with a line under 'ext'. The three titles carry no horizontal strike-through; each is underlined. The crossing strokes are large curves and verticals, unlike the wavy cancellation line used at c. 38(1). It is therefore unresolved whether they cancel, link or mark an insertion. The meaning of 'ext' is unresolved.
